limitations: Synthetic, author-labeled corpus; no independent expert validation.
Recall is measured per playbook rule, not every possible legal issue.
Exact quotations verify provenance, not interpretation or completeness.
Provider failures count as missed expected rules; they are not discarded.

findings.title: Early non-renewal deadline
findings.quote: The agreement rolls over into another annual term unless Vale delivers notice of non-renewal at least sixty-one days before expiry.
findings.rationale: Non-renewal requires 61 days of notice before renewal, exceeding the playbook maximum of 60 days.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may prevent automatic renewal by giving written notice at least sixty days before the renewal date.

findings.title: Data deletion period exceeds playbook
findings.quote: After the contract ends, Alder Archive must erase all customer files within 31 days.
findings.rationale: The deletion period is 31 days after termination, exceeding the playbook maximum of 30 days. Subprocessor notice does not change this deadline.
findings.proposed_language: Supplier shall delete customer data within thirty days of termination and give prior written notice of new subprocessors.

findings.title: Supplier convenience termination notice period is insufficient.
findings.quote: Basin may terminate for convenience on 45 days of written notice; all prepaid fees are non-refundable even for services not delivered.
findings.rationale: The notice period of 45 days does not meet the required minimum of 30 days for supplier convenience termination.
findings.proposed_language: Basin may terminate for convenience on at least 30 days of written notice, and all unused prepaid fees must be refunded.

findings.title: Liability cap exceeds preferred duration
findings.quote: Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid over the preceding twenty-four months; neither party is liable for indirect or consequential damages.
findings.rationale: The liability cap is based on fees paid over the preceding twenty-four months, which exceeds the preferred duration of twelve months.
findings.proposed_language: Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid over the preceding twelve months; neither party is liable for indirect or consequential damages.
